full_query: A 1-year-old girl is brought to a neurologist due to increasing seizure frequency over the past 2 months. She recently underwent a neurology evaluation which revealed hypsarrhythmia on electroencephalography (EEG) with a mix of slow waves, multifocal spikes, and asynchrony. Her parents have noticed the patient occasionally stiffens and spreads her arms at home. She was born at 38-weeks gestational age without complications. She has no other medical problems. Her medications consist of lamotrigine and valproic acid. Her temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 90/75 mmHg, pulse is 94/min, and respirations are 22/min. Physical exam reveals innumerable hypopigmented macules on the skin and an irregularly shaped, thickened, and elevated plaque on the lower back. Which of the following is most strongly associated with this patient's condition? (A) Cardiac rhabdomyoma (B) Glaucoma (C) Optic glioma (D) Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia (E) Renal cell carcinoma

Clinical presentation: The patient, a 1-year-old girl, has a history of increasing seizure frequency over the past 2 months
Her recent neurology evaluation revealed hypsarrhythmia on EEG with a mix of slow waves, multifocal spikes, and asynchrony
This presentation is characteristic of infantile spasms, also known as West syndrome, which is often associated with a poor developmental prognosis
Hypsarrhythmia on EEG is a hallmark of infantile spasms, characterized by high-amplitude, disorganized, and chaotic brain activity
Additional clinical findings: The patient's parents have noticed she occasionally stiffens and spreads her arms at home
This physical behavior is indicative of infantile spasms, which manifest as brief, involuntary muscle contractions, often involving the arms
Medical history: The patient was born at 38-weeks gestational age without complications
She has no other medical problems and is currently taking lamotrigine and valproic acid
These medications are antiepileptic drugs and are being used to manage the patient's seizures
There is no indication that they are contributing to her current condition
Physical examination findings: Innumerable hypopigmented macules on the skin and an irregularly shaped, thickened, and elevated plaque on the lower back were noted

The skin findings are suggestive of tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), a genetic disorder characterized by the growth of non-cancerous tumors in various organs, including the skin, brain, and other areas
Tuberous sclerosis complex is associated with a range of neurological manifestations, including seizures, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorders
Associations with Tuberous sclerosis complex: Tuberous sclerosis complex has been associated with cardiac rhabdomyoma, which is a type of benign heart tumor
